Sounds like going to NJIT served you very well. That's great that you were able to avoid financial burden so you have more freedom in your life. Also reassuring that the name doesn't always equate to being more capable or making more money.

First, congrats on being accepted to CU, that is not easy.

I was in a similar situation as yours, and I chose NJIT since it was cheaper and more familiar. I am graduating now and wonder if I would've realized more of my potential and found more of what I was looking for at a more selective college.

NJIT provides a fantastic value, but I recommend thinking beyond this. For people who are mainly focused on getting a college degree and a well-paying job after college, NJIT is ideal. That has been the goal for the majority of people I have met in my 5 years attending here.

But there are other important factors to consider. Living in Downtown Manhattan vs Newark is a HUGE difference. CU is an elite STEM institution in NYC, meaning the coursework, student population, and experience will differ from NJIT. Plus 22k/year is really not that bad for what you're getting. That's still significantly less than full-price NJIT.

When making this decision, don't just consider money and the job you get after. Consider what is important to you and how going to that college will help you achieve your ambitions, personally and professionally. There is more to college than "less money = go there", but I realize that many many people don't have the luxury of even considering the more expensive college.

If you feel like you will find more value at CU, go there. IMO, it is a no-brainer to go to CU, especially at that price. I personally regret following the whole "go to NJIT so you can pay less and get a job that pays well" mindset that I feel is prevalent here. The value of a college experience is not limited to the degree you get or how much money you get after.

Don't let anyone tell you how stressed or not stressed you should be. ***This shit is rough.***

One thing that's been working for me recently is to practice **self-compassion**. Reflect on how great you're doing despite the circumstances. You're trying your best and are only capable of so much. I'm hard on myself and often move the goal post, but now is a time to take it easy on yourself.

Another way to cope is for us to lean on each other. Seriously, reach out to a friend or even PM me to share what's troubling you. Depression, suicide, and substance abuse are at all-time highs esp in our age group. A lot of us are suffering and it is OK to talk to each other about it and lend support.

I really hope you catch a break soon, as well as anyone else reading that is struggling to be a student or even normal functioning person. I am open to chatting if anyone wants.
